Q: git fetch origin master:master does not advance origin/master, but it does advance FETCH_HEAD A:

It only works if master can be fast-forwarded.
If master has diverged, git fetch will not rewrite it unless you force it.

Update the remote-tracking branch:

git fetch origin master

# then force update (dangerous though)

git fetch origin +master:master

origin/master is not the remote’s master, its a local ref updated only by the remote’s fetch refspec, master:master never touches it.

Q: Node testing, "--test-name-pattern" parameter does not work A:

The issue is probably the order of your arguments.

The order should be:

node [options] [script.js] [arguments]

but because your option

--test-name-pattern="test [1-3]"

comes after your script, it's being treated as an argument for your sample.test.js so it gets ignored.

Try running your test with the proper order of arguments:

  • --test : option

  • --test-name-pattern="test [1-3]" : option

  • sample.test.js : script

Try the following, and it should work:

node --test --test-name-pattern="test [1-3]" Tests/sample.test.js

printWorkingDirectory()

Returns the pathname of the current working directory. Here's the reference.

Q: Filter by group value A:

SELECT * FROM link WHERE ID NOT IN (SELECT ID FROM link WHERE STATUS = 'error' AND ID IS NOT NULL);
